title: A refused Joomla import sign-in says Joomla needs the username, not the email; the operator signal records whether the username was an email and how the run came in, never the value
steps: S1: Pick the sentence for invalid_credential with importErrorKey (packages/site/tracy-add-site/src/client/refusal.tsx) for a Joomla run, a WordPress run, a Joomla run whose refusal Tracy could not read (check message_unread), and no_backend_access on Joomla.
S2: Follow a run in the import wizard that ends with error invalid_credential on Joomla.

S3: Run a WordPress import with fetch mocked so the login POST answers 'The password you entered for the username is incorrect', once with username owner@shop.example and once with shopowner; read the run state and the queued operation result.
S4: Call run.signInRefusal and run.signInWay directly for account refusals, front-of-account refusals (admin_gate, mfa_required) and the three ways a run gets the code (password, pasted code, saved).

S5: Sanitize a diagnostic carrying username_is_email (and a stray sign_in) with tracy-web importDiagnostic, including a string username_is_email, an extra username field and an unknown sign_in, then render it with signalText.

S6: Run an import with neither a login nor a pasted code and nothing kept, so it fails with no diagnostic; post to tracy-web's import-result door a call_failed result with sign_in and no detail, one with an unknown sign_in, and a done result with sign_in.
expect: S1: Joomla gets import_error_invalid_credential_joomla; WordPress keeps import_error_invalid_credential; message_unread stays import_error_signin_unclear; no_backend_access keeps its own sentence.
S2: the wizard shows the Joomla sentence.

S3: diagnostic is {at: login_post, check: invalid_credential, username_is_email: true|false}; the queued report carries sign_in: password beside that detail; neither the run state nor the report contains the username.
S4: only invalid_credential and no_backend_access gain username_is_email; owner@localhost is not an email shape; signInWay returns password, code, saved.

S5: a boolean username_is_email survives, everything else (including sign_in, which belongs to the result) is dropped; importSignIn keeps only password/code/saved; the alert ends with 'Sign-in: password · username is an email address' and contains no @.

S6: the queued report carries sign_in saved and no detail; the stored site.stuck row keeps sign_in and has no detail, its alert ends 'Reason: call_failed\nSign-in: password' with no Where line; an unknown sign_in is not stored; the site.result row keeps sign_in.

selectors.code: refusal.tsx importErrorKey, import-wizard.tsx errorDetail.platform, run.ts signInRefusal/signInWay, diagnostic.mjs usernameIsEmail/DIAGNOSTIC_SIGN_INS, apps/tracy-web/src/lib/import-diagnostic.js importSignIn, sites/route.js import-result, ops-signal.js signIn

evidence: A production Joomla customer's import stopped on invalid_credential (Joomla: 'Username and password do not match'); the customer most likely typed the email address, which Joomla's backend does not accept, and the sentence did not say so
fence: the Joomla sentence for invalid_credential and the username_is_email/sign_in fields of the import diagnostic

tests: a wrong password on Joomla says Joomla needs the username; WordPress keeps its sentence
a refused WordPress sign-in reports whether the username was an email and how the run came in, never the username
signInRefusal marks only a refused account, and signInWay names how the run came in
a run that fails with no diagnostic still reports how it came in, and no made-up detail
